name: Hyrox — Intermediate

workouts.name: 8km Easy + 6 Strides
workouts.description: Easy run finishing with short strides to develop running economy and neuromuscular coordination.
workouts.notes: Block opener, dialled back: HRV is reading unbalanced and training readiness is 44/100 right now, so this is easy running with a handful of relaxed strides instead of race-pace work — pure aerobic signal, no clock-watching. Full quality resumes with Friday's tempo.

workouts.name: 9km Easy Run
workouts.description: Relaxed aerobic run at conversational pace. Builds base fitness.
workouts.notes: Conversational pace throughout — if you can't chat in full sentences, slow down. This sets the aerobic rhythm the rest of the block builds on.

workouts.name: 5km Tempo Run
workouts.description: Sustained threshold-pace effort. Develops lactate clearance and mental focus.
workouts.notes: 20 minutes continuous at threshold, 'comfortably hard' — controlled, not a race. First real lactate-clearance stimulus of the block, so respect the pace zone rather than chasing a number.

workouts.name: 9km Long Run
workouts.description: Steady long run building endurance and mental toughness at easy pace.
workouts.notes: Steady and easy end to end. Focus on posture and cadence in the second half rather than pace — this is about time on feet, not speed.

workouts.name: 10 x 60s Hill Reps
workouts.description: Hill repetitions build strength, power, and running economy. Effort should be hard but controlled.
workouts.notes: Hard uphill effort for 60s, jog back down for recovery — chase power and knee drive, not pace. Hills build strength without the pounding of flat speedwork.

workouts.name: 9km Easy + 6 Strides
workouts.description: Easy run finishing with short strides to develop running economy and neuromuscular coordination.
workouts.notes: Easy running finished with 6 relaxed strides — quick legs, low effort, focus on smooth turnover rather than max speed.

workouts.name: 5km Progressive Run
workouts.description: Start easy, finish fast. Each third gets progressively faster developing pacing discipline.
workouts.notes: Each third gets faster — easy, then marathon effort, then threshold. A gentle taste of race-day pacing discipline.

workouts.name: 10km Long Run
workouts.description: Steady long run building endurance and mental toughness at easy pace.
workouts.notes: Easy pace, slightly longer than last week. Should feel like a natural progression, not a stretch.

workouts.name: 6 x 1.2km Race Pace Intervals
workouts.description: Race-specific intervals at threshold pace. Builds confidence and specificity.
workouts.notes: Longer reps than last time — 1.2km at threshold effort teaches you to hold race rhythm a little longer before the legs start arguing. Recovery jogs stay easy.

workouts.name: 10km Easy Run
workouts.description: Relaxed aerobic run at conversational pace. Builds base fitness.
workouts.notes: Relaxed effort — this is recovery from Tuesday's intervals as much as it is aerobic work.

workouts.name: 6km Tempo Run
workouts.description: Sustained threshold-pace effort. Develops lactate clearance and mental focus.
workouts.notes: Threshold effort, ~24 minutes continuous. Should feel 'comfortably hard' the whole way — if the last 2km feel easy, you went out too conservatively.

workouts.name: 10km Progressive Long Run
workouts.description: Start easy, build to marathon pace, finish at threshold. Develops pacing and fatigue resistance.
workouts.notes: Easy first 60%, marathon effort for the next 30%, threshold to finish. Mental toughness session — the last kilometres are meant to hurt a little.

workouts.name: 8 x 45s Hill Reps
workouts.description: Hill repetitions build strength, power, and running economy. Effort should be hard but controlled.
workouts.notes: Shorter hill reps this week, fewer minutes of hard work — keep the stimulus without adding fatigue during the cutback.

workouts.name: 8km Easy + 6 Strides
workouts.description: Easy run finishing with short strides to develop running economy and neuromuscular coordination.
workouts.notes: Easy volume trimmed back this week — let the legs recover while the strides keep turnover sharp.

workouts.name: 6 x 0.6km Race Pace Intervals
workouts.description: Race-specific intervals at threshold pace. Builds confidence and specificity.
workouts.notes: Short, sharp 600m reps at threshold — enough race-rhythm practice to stay sharp without loading the legs during the down week.

workouts.name: 8km Long Run
workouts.description: Steady long run building endurance and mental toughness at easy pace.
workouts.notes: Shorter long run — this is a deliberate down week. Trust it; the next block builds off a fresher body.

workouts.name: 5 x 1.4km Race Pace Intervals
workouts.description: Race-specific intervals at threshold pace. Builds confidence and specificity.
workouts.notes: Reps stretch out to 1.4km — longer than the base phase, closer to sustained race rhythm. Same threshold effort, just held a little longer each time.

workouts.name: 11km Easy Run
workouts.description: Relaxed aerobic run at conversational pace. Builds base fitness.
workouts.notes: Easy effort, building volume again after the cutback. Should feel comfortably fresh.

workouts.name: 6km Tempo Run
workouts.description: Sustained threshold-pace effort. Develops lactate clearance and mental focus.
workouts.notes: ~24 minutes at threshold. This is the lactate-clearance workhorse of the build phase — hold it steady, don't surge.

workouts.name: 11km Long Run w/ 3km Race Pace
workouts.description: Long run with a sustained race-pace block to build specificity and confidence.
workouts.notes: Easy through the middle, then 3km at race effort near the end — first taste of running your target pace on tired-ish legs.

workouts.name: 6 x 3.5min VO2max Intervals
workouts.description: Hard intervals at VO2max intensity to raise aerobic ceiling. Full recovery between reps.
workouts.notes: Hard efforts at your aerobic ceiling with equal-time jog recovery. These should hurt by rep 4 — that's the point, it's raising your VO2max.

workouts.name: 11km Easy + 6 Strides
workouts.description: Easy run finishing with short strides to develop running economy and neuromuscular coordination.
workouts.notes: Easy volume with a few quick strides at the end — legs should feel lively, not tired, coming out of Tuesday's VO2max work.

workouts.name: 5 x 7min Cruise Intervals
workouts.description: Broken threshold work with short recoveries. Same lactate benefit as tempo with less mental fatigue.
workouts.notes: Broken tempo — 7-minute reps at threshold with a short jog between. Same lactate benefit as a continuous tempo, easier to hold the pace.

workouts.name: 12km Progressive Long Run
workouts.description: Start easy, build to marathon pace, finish at threshold. Develops pacing and fatigue resistance.
workouts.notes: Biggest long run of the block so far. Easy, then marathon effort, then threshold to close — pacing discipline under real fatigue.

workouts.name: 4 x 1.8km Race Pace Intervals
workouts.description: Race-specific intervals at threshold pace. Builds confidence and specificity.
workouts.notes: Longest race-pace reps yet — 1.8km blocks at threshold, closer to unbroken race rhythm than anything so far this block.

workouts.name: 12km Easy Run
workouts.description: Relaxed aerobic run at conversational pace. Builds base fitness.
workouts.notes: Easy effort — biggest easy run of the plan. Patience over pace.

workouts.name: 6km Progressive Run
workouts.description: Start easy, finish fast. Each third gets progressively faster developing pacing discipline.
workouts.notes: Three even thirds — easy, marathon, threshold. A tune-up for pacing discipline before the weekend's long run.

workouts.name: 13km Long Run w/ 3km Race Pace
workouts.description: Long run with a sustained race-pace block to build specificity and confidence.
workouts.notes: Longest run of the plan, finishing with 3km at race pace on tired legs — the single best predictor session for how race day will feel.

workouts.name: 6 x 0.8km Race Pace Intervals
workouts.description: Race-specific intervals at threshold pace. Builds confidence and specificity.
workouts.notes: Shorter, crisper reps — 800m at threshold. Sharpening, not grinding; this should feel controlled, even good.

workouts.name: 9km Easy + 6 Strides
workouts.description: Easy run finishing with short strides to develop running economy and neuromuscular coordination.
workouts.notes: Easy running with strides — keep the legs moving without digging any fatigue hole this close to taper.

workouts.name: 3 x 1.5km Race Pace Intervals
workouts.description: Race-specific intervals at threshold pace. Builds confidence and specificity.
workouts.notes: Just 3 reps at 1.5km — race rhythm rehearsal, minimal volume. Confidence work, not conditioning work.

workouts.name: 10km Long Run
workouts.description: Steady long run building endurance and mental toughness at easy pace.
workouts.notes: Easy and comfortable. Volume is coming down — protect freshness over fitness gains from here.

workouts.name: 5 x 1.6km Race Pace Intervals
workouts.description: Race-specific intervals at threshold pace. Builds confidence and specificity.
workouts.notes: Longest race-pace reps of the whole plan — 1.6km blocks at threshold. This is the confidence session: if these feel controlled, you're ready.

workouts.name: 13km Easy Run
workouts.description: Relaxed aerobic run at conversational pace. Builds base fitness.
workouts.notes: Easy pace, biggest easy run of the plan. Last big aerobic top-up before the taper starts.

workouts.name: 4 x 8min Cruise Intervals
workouts.description: Broken threshold work with short recoveries. Same lactate benefit as tempo with less mental fatigue.
workouts.notes: Longer, fewer reps than earlier cruise-interval sessions — 8-minute blocks at threshold. Sustained control over raw volume.

workouts.name: 14km Progressive Long Run
workouts.description: Start easy, build to marathon pace, finish at threshold. Develops pacing and fatigue resistance.
workouts.notes: Longest run of the entire plan — easy, marathon effort, then threshold to finish. After this, everything is taper.

workouts.name: Easy shakeout
workouts.description: Easy shakeout
workouts.notes: Just enough to keep the legs moving — very easy, short. You're not fitter by race day because of this run; you're only less fresh if you push it.

workouts.name: Light strides
workouts.description: Light strides
workouts.notes: A handful of relaxed strides to wake the legs up, nothing more. Then rest up — race day is 2026-11-13.

adaptation_notes: 2026-07-06: HRV is reading UNBALANCED and training readiness is 44/100 — softened Week 1's opening session (race-pace intervals -> easy run w/ strides) so the block starts once current fatigue has been absorbed. Also added variety: race-pace rep lengths now range 0.6-1.8km instead of a flat 1.0km, tempo/threshold sessions land in the 20-30min zone, and Week 5's long run gets a race-pace finish.
